audit.whatIsWrong: content.late and wants.foe[2] both say Shapesplitter's clone baits 'your telegraphed R onto the wrong target'.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force launches Malphite to a location — it is not unit-targeted, so there is no wrong target to be tricked into. The clone's actual cost to Malphite is that he spends a 130s ultimate arriving at empty ground. Same warning, correct mechanism, and the corrected version tells the player what to actually look at.

audit.whatIsWrong: Tangle-Barbs is treated as chip damage and a root to bait, and its range is never given.
audit.why: Tangle-Barbs roots at 1000 units. Unstoppable Force travels 1000 units. Those are the same number, and a root prevents a dash outright — so this matchup at 6 is a single question of who casts first, on a 12s cooldown against a 130s one. That asymmetry is the most important thing on the page and it was not there.
audit.corrected: Tangle-Barbs roots at 1000, your R travels 1000, and a root cancels a dash — 12s against 130s, so cast first or not at all.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page warns about the clone but never mentions the disguise's effect on Pop Blossom.
audit.why: Riot's own Pop Blossom text ends 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised.' That is a hidden-mechanic tell straight from the ability description rather than a community claim: against a disguised Neeko there is no visible wind-up to react to, which is exactly the read a Malphite needs before he walks into a group.
audit.corrected: Pop Blossom's preparation is hidden while she is disguised — a Neeko who looks like an ally may already be charging it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Blooming Burst's second bloom is described only as 'her Q bounces off minions hit me twice'.
audit.why: Riot's text is specific: the seed blooms again on hitting champions or killing units. So the danger is not a bounce off minions in general, it is standing where a dying minion triggers the re-bloom on top of you. Naming the trigger makes the positioning rule actionable instead of vague.
audit.corrected: Blooming Burst blooms a second time when it hits a champion or kills a unit — don't last-hit standing inside it.

audit.why: Tangle-Barbs 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, Blooming Burst 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, Pop Blossom 120/105/90. The root's ten-to-twelve seconds is the only window in which Malphite's dash is guaranteed to arrive, and it was not written down anywhere.
